🇺🇸 The US midterms changed how Washington works. Before vs after, explained 👇

BEFORE: Republicans controlled the House, the Senate (53-47) and the White House. President Trump could pass laws with his own party's votes.

AFTER (from 3 January 2027): Democrats control both houses. Projections give them roughly 245-258 of 435 House seats and a Senate majority of at least 51 of 100 seats. Mississippi (a 43-vote gap) and Alaska are still being counted. Trump stays president until January 2029.

What changes:
📜 New laws: need both houses AND the president's signature, so Trump's agenda largely stops, and he can veto Democrat bills. Overriding a veto needs two-thirds of both houses, which Democrats don't have.
💰 Money: all spending bills start in the House. Expect fights over the budget, government shutdown deadlines and the debt limit.
🔎 Oversight: the majority chairs every committee, so Democrats can call hearings, subpoena officials and investigate the administration.
⚖️ Appointments: the Senate approves judges, cabinet members and ambassadors. Trump's nominees now need Democrat votes.
🏛️ Impeachment: the House can impeach with a simple majority, but removal needs 67 senators.
🌍 Trade: Congress controls trade law, including AGOA's renewal, but the president keeps many tariff powers he uses by executive action.

What stays the same: Trump can still sign executive orders, direct foreign policy and set many tariffs.

Why it matters for Mzansi: AGOA, tariffs and US aid are now negotiated with a split government, which can mean more checks, but also more gridlock.

Do you think a divided Washington is good or bad for South Africa? 👇
